value: other waterfowl of the family Anatidae
carried by migratory waterfowl that show no symptoms

mortality.value: can reach up to 90 percent, with death usually within 5 days of symptoms starting

incubation_period.value: 3 to 7 days in domestic waterfowl, up to 14 days in wild waterfowl

diagnosis.value: based on clinical signs and post-mortem findings such as small bleeding spots in mucous membranes and organs, confirmed with tissue or antigen testing

value: keeping birds away from wild waterfowl and contaminated water
screening new birds before adding them to a flock

treatment_overview.value: there is no treatment; outbreaks are managed by removing and isolating birds and thorough disinfection

summary.value: Duck plague is a highly fatal viral disease of ducks, geese and swans that spreads through contaminated water and direct contact, with migratory waterfowl often carrying it without symptoms. It is not known to infect chickens or humans, and prevention relies on vaccination and keeping flocks away from wild waterfowl.
